description: Leave conversion pay (monetised leave) is taxed at year end exactly as the cutoff taxed it. The cutoff withholds on a conversion marked tax exempt as if it were not paid, and on a taxable one as ordinary pay. Year-end annualization must do the same: a LEAVE_CONV- line carrying 'Tax treatment: exempt' joins the non-taxable bucket, a taxable one stays in taxable income. Phase 27 certifies it through the real engine with four workers hired at the switch on the same salary: a control, an exempt conversion in cutoff 13, a taxable conversion in cutoff 13, and an exempt conversion in cutoff 13 plus a taxable one in cutoff 14. Statutory contributions are unaffected because the 60,000 salary is already at the SSS and Pag-IBIG ceilings and PhilHealth is on basic salary only.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (up to 10,417 exempt; 10,417 to 16,667: 15%; 16,667 to 33,333: 937.50 + 20%; over 33,333: 4,270.70 + 25% of the excess); annual table (up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000 to 400,000: 15% of the excess over 250,000). Monetised unused vacation and sick leave of up to 10 days is exempt (RR 8-2018, NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) and its regulations); a conversion the employer marks taxable is compensation income.
sources.thirteenthMonth: Presidential Decree 851: 13th month pay = one twelfth of basic salary earned in the year; exempt up to 90,000 together with other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)). Monetised leave is not basic salary and does not enter the 13th month.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing, monthly salary 60,000 (30,000 a cutoff), every worker hired 2026-07-01 so only the 12 engine cutoffs 13-24 exist and there are no imported rows. An ordinary cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 100 (1,725); taxable 30,000 - 1,725 = 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 0.20 x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10; net 25,015.90.

A conversion is 5 days of Vacation Leave at a daily rate of 2,000.00 = 10,000.00, approved just before its cutoff and marked paid after it (which is what release settlement does). Cutoff gross becomes 40,000 and the SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG amounts do not change.

Year end for a worker with no 13th month paid: entries 12 x 30,000 plus the conversions; entitlement = basic earned 360,000 / 12 = 30,000 accrued unpaid and added to gross compensation; contributions 12 x 1,725 = 20,700; the 30,000 sits inside the 90,000 pool; non-taxable = pool + contributions + exempt conversions; taxable = gross - non-taxable; tax = 15% x (taxable - 250,000); withheld = the sum of the WHT lines only; a refund is a negative adjustment.

noConversionControl.description: No conversion. Net pay 25,015.90 in every cutoff. Year end: gross 390,000; non-taxable 50,700; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; withheld 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20.

exemptConversion.description: An exempt 10,000.00 conversion in cutoff 13. The cutoff withholds as if it were not paid, so year end must exclude it too: gross 400,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 + 10,000 = 60,700; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; withheld 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20, identical to the control. If year end taxed it the refund would be 1,500.00 too small.

taxableConversion.description: A taxable 10,000.00 conversion in cutoff 13. The cutoff withholds 5,506.20 (2,247.10 more than an ordinary cutoff) and year end keeps it in taxable income: gross 400,000; non-taxable 50,700; taxable 349,300; tax 15% x 99,300 = 14,895.00; withheld 11 x 3,259.10 + 5,506.20 = 41,356.30; refund 26,461.30.

exemptThenTaxableConversion.description: An exempt 10,000.00 conversion in cutoff 13 and a taxable 10,000.00 conversion in cutoff 14. Cutoff 13 withholds 3,259.10 and cutoff 14 5,506.20. Year end: gross 410,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 + 10,000 = 60,700; taxable 349,300; tax 14,895.00; withheld 10 x 3,259.10 + 3,259.10 + 5,506.20 = 41,356.30; refund 26,461.30. Each conversion keeps its own treatment.

limitations: Only Vacation Leave conversions of 5 days, in cutoffs 13 and 14, are exercised. Whether the exempt day limit is respected is a policy input chosen when the conversion is approved and is not tested here.
Company premium rules (PREM-, OTPREM-, NDPREM-, DAYPREM-) at year end are not exercised; they need pay policy setup.
One salary, 'split' timing, a worker hired at the switch (no imported history), contributions at their ceilings.
Final pay (separation) derives year-to-date gross from released gross pay and is not exercised here; see Phase 25.
Year-end rows already computed under an older rule are replaced only when year end is recomputed.
